definition: Preconception refers to the period before a pregnancy begins. In this context, it is the time when a mother’s or father’s health, behaviors, medications, substance use, mental health, and environmental exposures may influence pregnancy outcomes such as infant birth weight.

reasons: The definition broadens the packet’s scope by asserting a general sense of “preconception” as the period before pregnancy begins; the packet only uses “preconception period” in the context of preconception health/care and does not explicitly define the term.

It overgeneralizes from the packet by attributing to both mothers and fathers a broad list of health factors (behaviors, medications, substance use, mental health, environmental exposures) and their effects on pregnancy outcomes; the packet supports only specific maternal preconception health and several paternal factors in relation to infant birth weight, not this generalized formulation.
The packet uses the term “preconception period” but does not explicitly define it as “the period before a pregnancy begins,” so the definition’s first clause is not directly supported.

The definition claims these factors “may influence pregnancy outcomes”; the packet specifically discusses associations with infant birth weight (and paternal preconception factors), but does not substantiate broader “pregnancy outcomes” beyond examples centered on birth weight.
